To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Monte Amiato ore district (Italy) is characterized by high concentrations of Hg, Sb and As in soils, which is a consequence of ore mining and processing activity.
Hg, As, Sb contents and fractionation were investigated in soil and waste samples from the former ASS mining site of the M. Amiata ore distric (Italy).

(1) ore processing activities provided a contribution to the Hg contamination and fractionation of the soils in the roasting zone, (2) the Hg fractionation pattern suggested the presence of volatile Hg species, and (3) Sb and As were mainly in residual fraction in all soil and waste sample.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the influence of ore processing activity and the geochemical characteristics of the ore on Hg, Sb and As fractionation in soils and waste materials.

Hg contamination in soils and waste of the ASS mining site was mainly due to ore processing activities, while As and Sb contamination was mainly due to natural background.

Hg, Sb and As contamination levels and fractionation in soil and mining wastes at the ASS mining site depend on the different contribution of mining activities.
the ore processing activity at the ASS mining site influenced the distribution and availability of Hg in soils and mining waste.

Hg contamination and fractionation were mainly due to ore processing activities, while Sb and As contamination were mainly due to the presence in the ore and the use of pyrite as a flux in the metallurgical process.

the geochemical behaviour of Hg, Sb and As in the soil environment is strongly dependent on the type of mineral processing and on the type of soil and waste samples.
ore processing activities have a significant impact on the Hg contamination and fractionation of soils.
